checklist.fact: The RFP is issued by Empire State Development (ESD) through its Office of Strategic Workforce Development (OSWD), created after Governor Hochul's April 2022 announcement of $350 million for workforce development.
checklist.quote: In April 2022, Governor Kathy Hochul announced an investment of $350 million for workforce development, including the creation of the Office of Strategic Workforce Development (OSWD) within ESD.

checklist.fact: The need is that AI-related jobs often require specialized education and training out of reach for low-income individuals, creating a risk that AI progress will disproportionately benefit those already privileged and leave underrepresented communities behind.
checklist.quote: Many well-paying AI-related jobs require specialized education and technical training, which are often out of reach for lower-income individuals.

checklist.fact: AI Prep is an applied training program with two tracks: Track A (AI Prep 4 Internships) for low-income matriculating undergraduates seeking paid internships, and Track B (AI Prep 4 Jobs) for low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment via accelerated training or bootcamp.
checklist.quote: AI Prep will have two dedicated tracks to serve New Yorkers who are currently underrepresented in the tech industry and who cannot reasonably access training on their own.

checklist.fact: OSWD seeks to award contracts to up to two qualified program administrators to develop the curriculum for and administer AI Prep for Track A and/or Track B.
checklist.quote: OSWD seeks to award contracts to up to two (2) qualified program administrators to develop the curriculum for and to administer AI Prep for Track A and/or Track B.

checklist.fact: Funding is up to $2M per track (up to $4M total) for an initial term of up to 18 months, with possible renewal or extension based on performance, need, and availability of funds.
checklist.quote: ESD will invest up to $2M for each track (up to $4M total) to train and provide stipends for participating individuals.

checklist.fact: Budgets exceeding $2M for one track or $4M for both tracks over the contract period will not be considered, and indirect costs are not allowable.
checklist.quote: Budgets exceeding $2M for one track or $4M for both tracks for the total contract period will not be considered.

checklist.fact: Program objectives require serving a minimum of 250 participants (priority for those serving more than 400), with over 50% low-income participants.
checklist.quote: Should serve a minimum of 250 participants with priority for applicants that serve more than 400 participants.

checklist.fact: Most graduates should secure paid internships or full-time employment in AI or a closely related field.
checklist.quote: The majority of individuals who complete the program ("graduates") should secure paid internships or full-time employment in artificial intelligence or a closely related field.

checklist.fact: Applicants may be non-profit or for-profit and must have experience in at least three of four domains: academic services to college students, high-tech accelerated training, serving low-income populations, and working in the New York market.
checklist.quote: Applicants must have experience in at least three of the four following domains to qualify to administer the program:

checklist.fact: Proposals are due by 2:00 PM ET on October 1, 2025, uploaded to a designated Dropbox; late proposals will not be accepted.
checklist.quote: Submission Deadline: 2:00 PM ET on October 1, 2025

checklist.fact: The anticipated schedule is: winner announced November 14, 2025, and contract start January 1, 2026.
